claim: Diario de Pernambuco reported on 23 June 2026 that Porto Digital's Cais do Porto unit in Aveiro has been active since 2024 and that more than 45 Brazilian companies, most from Pernambuco, have used it.
DN Brasil reported on 22 June 2026 that a second group of ten Pernambuco companies arrived in June 2026 through Porto Digital's internationalisation programme.
On 30 June 2026, Porto Digital, Cais do Porto and CONSECTI signed a cooperation agreement, as reported by TI Inside.
In November 2024, Brazil's ambassador to Portugal, Raimundo Carreiro Silva, wrote in DN that Porto Digital Europa had chosen Aveiro's innovation hub and already had ten companies on board.
On 13 November 2023, during Web Summit, Sebrae's president, Décio Lima, signed a memorandum of understanding with Startup Portugal.
Unicorn Factory Lisboa has signed partnerships with three Brazilian hubs: Instituto Caldeira (Porto Alegre), Cubo (São Paulo) and Sai do Papel.
Gil Azevedo, head of Unicorn Factory Lisboa, told ECO in April 2025 that the city's innovation hub had three partnerships signed with Brazilian hubs.
ApexBrasil reports Brazil's ecosystem as 13,000 startups, more than 120 venture capital funds, more than 250 innovation hubs and more than 30 unicorns.
Brasil 61 reported on 31 August 2026 that Brazil raised US$2.135 billion in venture capital in 2024 across 386 deals.
The ApexBrasil and Sebrae Lisbon incubator's first class of ten startups was named at Web Summit 2025, and its 2027 class is due to be announced at the Brazil Pavilion on 10 November.
Brazil's pavilion at Web Summit lasts three days.
Gol has opened its first intercontinental route, from Rio de Janeiro to Lisbon.
